primitives.name: Disguise Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — port the "disguise rate" (pre-snap vs post-snap assignment divergence) and per-defender matchup-attribution concepts to GSE's matchup model using Big Data Bowl 2025 tracking; the proprietary NGS/PFF labels cannot be replicated.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Δt': 'time interval (seconds)', 'A_{pre}': 'assignment vector pre-snap (dimension d)', 'A_{post}': 'assignment vector post-snap (dimension d)', 'R': 'disguise rate = ||A_{post} - A_{pre}||_2 / ||A_{pre}||_2'}
primitives.assumptions: Assignments are represented as dense vectors; temporal divergence is measured via L2 norm.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High disguise rates indicate dynamic coverage shifts or misalignment between pre-snap and actual play execution.

layer2.mapping: Disguise rate maps to a change detection signal in GSE's state transition engine, where Δt represents the temporal window of assignment evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Play-level variance in defender assignment vectors before and after snap.

primitives.name: Matchup Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — port the "disguise rate" (pre-snap vs post-snap assignment divergence) and per-defender matchup-attribution concepts to GSE's matchup model using Big Data Bowl 2025 tracking; the proprietary NGS/PFF labels cannot be replicated.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{ij}': 'matchup score between defender i and receiver j (dimension k)', 'P_i': "defender i's positional embedding (dimension d)", 'R_j': "receiver j's positional embedding (dimension d)", 'A_{ij}': 'attribution matrix element = P_i \\cdot R_j'}
primitives.assumptions: Matchups are modeled as inner products of learned embeddings; attribution is symmetric and normalized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low attribution scores suggest weak or non-existent matchup alignment.

layer2.mapping: Matchup attribution forms a kernel in GSE's relational reasoning layer, enabling pairwise defender-receiver compatibility scoring.
layer2.telemetry: Per-defender receiver assignment probabilities from softmax over matchup scores.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_s': 'coverage scheme label (categorical, 20 classes)', 'F_s': 'situational features vector (dimension m)', 'Z_t': 'transformer output representation at time t (dimension d)', 'L_{cov}': 'coverage loss function (cross-entropy)'}
primitives.assumptions: Coverage schemes are discrete and temporally stable; situational features are static during play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coverage assignment fails when situational context is ambiguous or when scheme prediction is inaccurate.

layer2.mapping: Coverage assignment classifier in GSI maps to a GSE policy engine that selects coverage schemes based on contextual features and predicted play outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of coverage scheme predictions across play types.

The disguise rate primitive captures how much defensive assignments shift post-snap, which is critical for understanding coverage adaptability. Matchup attribution uses learned embeddings to compute compatibility between defenders and receivers, forming a kernel for relational reasoning. Coverage assignment classifiers integrate situational context with transformer outputs to predict team-level coverage schemes. These primitives are unified under a shared factorized attention framework that enables multi-task learning while preserving interpretability. Dualities emerge in that disguise rate and matchup attribution both reflect dynamic assignment changes, whereas coverage assignment reflects strategic planning. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited public datasets, leakage from temporal augmentation, and poor generalization to rare coverage schemes.
